afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 152320
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
420 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026

.UPDATE...00Z Aviation Discussion

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Wind advisories in effect tonight through Saturday morning
  across southern Arizona and southeast California, with breezy 
  to windy conditions expected as forecast peak wind gusts reach 
  up to 40-55 mph.

- Strong winds on Friday will likely lead to widespread lofted
  dust, leading to hazy conditions, and localized dust channels
  occasionally reducing visibility below one mile.

- Dry weather with near normal temperatures the next couple days,
  then slightly cooler with a slight chances for rain showers this
  weekend.
  
- A Pacific low pressure system moving down the coast early next
  week is currently forecast to bring regional rain chances, 
  breezy conditions, and cooler temperatures by the middle to 
  latter portions of next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/... 
Dry conditions under clear skies continue across the area today. 
Synoptically a blocking pattern is developing with high pressure 
ridging spreading into the Northwest CONUS and a developing weak 
cutoff low south of it over the local area. Despite the developing
cutoff low, H5 heights have risen over the last 24 hours and 
temperatures have warmed 5-10 degrees across southern AZ and 
southeast CA. High temperatures this afternoon are forecast to 
reach the mid to upper 80s and there is around a 60-70% chance of 
reaching 90 degrees in Phoenix. High temperatures tomorrow will 
be similar to today, except for the western deserts where it will 
be a few degrees warmer, reaching the low 90s. Temperatures then 
cool down again for Saturday with an increase in clouds, possibly 
some light showers/virga, and cold air advection from the east. 

The main sensible weather impact the next few days will be the 
wind and perhaps a lot of lofted dust as a result. This may be one
of the the strongest easterly gradient wind events of the last 
decade. Surface analysis at midday today showed a strong 
1040-1042mb high centered over Montana, which is near record 
strength for this time of year. The pressure gradient between the 
strong high to the north and the lower pressure over the local 
area is leading to breezy to locally windy conditions across 
northern AZ and across parts of southeast CA this afternoon. Wind 
gusts were consistently reaching 35-40 mph across these areas 
early this afternoon. As the strong surface high spreads further 
into the Plains and south along the southern Rockies, the pressure
gradient will continue to increase across the local area and as a
result so will the winds. A strong cold front moving south 
through the Plains will backdoor into southern AZ tonight/tomorrow
morning. Models continue to show 850mb LLJ winds reaching 40-50 
kts over south-central AZ early tomorrow morning, and even upwards
of 60 kts across southeast AZ. While these winds are not expected
to fully mix to the surface, the strong gradient will still lead 
to widespread 20-25 mph sustained and 30-40 mph wind gusts. Higher
peak wind gusts up to 45-50 mph are expected, with locally up to 
55 mph over mountain peaks, but the window for these stronger 
gusts will mostly be in the morning tomorrow and again Saturday 
morning. Winds this strong will surely kick up a lot of dust and 
create hazy conditions, and will likely lead to some dust channels
developing, with reduction in visibilities to under 1 mile at 
times, depending on land use. 

Wind advisories will be in effect for this wind event, 
starting initially this evening across southeast CA and along the
Lower Colorado River Valley with 35-45 mph northerly winds. 
Southwest and south-central AZ are then added to the advisory 
tomorrow morning. The decision was made to add the greater Phoenix
area to the advisory for a period from 8 AM - 3 PM MST. During 
this period, model soundings show potential for 30-35 kt (35-40 
mph) to mix down to the surface. The advisory for Pinal and 
southern Gila counties will continue through Saturday morning, as 
the easterly LLJ restrengthens overnight, and portions of 
southwest AZ will likely be re-added the advisory for Saturday 
morning as well.

As mentioned there will be an increase in clouds Saturday, as 
moisture is drawn north into the area by the weak cutoff low to 
the southwest. Vertical cross-sections and model soundings show 
this moisture will mostly be focused aloft between 700-300mb with 
a dry sub-cloud layer. Still, soundings suggest thick clouds with 
potential for light showers and virga beginning around midday and 
heading into the afternoon Saturday. Model guidance also shows a 
wing of vorticity or shortwave trough moving up from the south 
Saturday, with an enhancement to the upper level jet. This should 
provide decent ascent over southern AZ and further support at 
least light shower/virga activity. NBM PoPs Saturday are only
around 10-20% across south-central AZ (30% east of Phoenix) and
QPF is very light with NBM 75th percentile only showing 0.01" for
Phoenix to 0.10" for southern Gila County.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
The strong pressure gradient and resultant strong easterly winds 
across southern AZ will weaken heading into Sunday as the strong
surface high in the Plains weakens and shifts to the Mid-Atlantic.
There will still be some easterly breeziness, but nowhere near the
magnitude of Friday through Saturday. The synoptic pattern will
also shift, with the ridge over the Northwest CONUS sliding east
through the Plains and the cutoff low will also weaken into an
open wave and lift through the area Sunday-Monday, downstream of
the next Fall trough digging down the West Coast.

Lingering light showers are possible across portions of AZ, mainly
east and southeast AZ, Sunday into the start of next week 
downstream of the lingering shortwave trough, but drier air is 
shown to move in aloft prior to the arrival of the next coastal
trough. Temperatures should warm Sunday into the start of next
week with the latest NBM showing highs returning back close to
normal by Monday.

Tuesday through the middle of next week forecast confidence
decreases as model spread increases considerably. Most notably
there is a lot of model disagreement on timing out when the
coastal trough will move inland, how quickly, and how deep the
trough will be. Typically models will trend toward the slower
solutions with these coastal lows. So, something moving through
late week is the current thinking. This next coastal trough will 
bring chances for rain, breezy winds, and cooler temperatures, but
to what magnitude is still uncertain.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2320Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
The main aviation concerns during the TAF period will be breezy 
to windy conditions along with lofted dust late Friday morning 
into the afternoon. In the meantime, NE flow will continue into 
the evening and overnight hours, with sporadic gusts seen 
throughout this timeframe, though confidence regarding what time 
and which location may experience these gusts is low. Regardless, 
sustained speeds will remain relatively elevated compared to what 
is typical, and stronger winds just above the surface may result 
in some localized LLWS criteria. The strongest gusts during the 
forecast window look likely to occur Friday morning, sometime 
between 16-20Z, with observations nearing 30-35 kt. These strong 
winds will be capable of producing BLDU which, in some instances, 
could drop surface VIS down to MVFR levels. Whether or not dust 
impacts are seen at the surface, confidence in lofted dust 
resulting in slantwise VIS issues through much of the daylight 
hours is much greater. Clear skies will prevail through Friday 
evening. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
Marginal breeziness will be the main aviation concern during the
next 24 hours, mainly during the daylight hours. However, some
sporadic gusts around 25 kt may be seen during the overnight,
mainly at KBLH. NW-NE flow will be common at each terminal through
Friday morning before directions take on a more NE/E direction by
beyond that. FEW to perhaps SCT mid-level cloud decks will develop
over the region during the back-half of the forecast. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Drier air will persist over the region over the next couple of days 
with mostly clear skies and seasonally low humidities. MinRHs 
will be between 15-30% across the region through Saturday. North
and northeasterly breezes up to 25-35 mph are expected through
this evening in portions of southeast CA and along the lower CO
River Valley, as well as in the mountains north and northeast of
of Phoenix. Winds turn easterly and become stronger tonight 
through Saturday across southern AZ. Winds will be strongest over
mountain tops during the overnight and early morning hours
tomorrow and Saturday, with gusts up to 50-55 mph. Strong gusty
winds will spread more to the lower deserts during the daylight
hours and be strongest in the morning through early afternoon
tomorrow, with gusts up to 40-45 mph. These strong easterlies and
20-25% RHs may still create locally elevated fire weather 
conditions midday through the afternoon tomorrow, but fuels are
not the most receptive after recent rains. The easterly breezes
will not be nearly as strong during the day Saturday and will
trend down further into Sunday. Light showers are possible this
weekend, but the chance for wetting rain is low (<10%). A Pacific
trough is expected to bring regional rain chances, breezy winds,
and cooler temperatures next week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...     Wind Advisory from 5 AM Friday to 11 AM MST Saturday for AZZ547-
     552-553-555-557-558-560>562.

     Wind Advisory from 8 PM this evening to 2 PM MST Friday for 
     AZZ530.

     Wind Advisory from 5 AM to 3 PM MST Friday for AZZ531>534-536-
     538-539-554-559.

     Wind Advisory from 8 AM to 3 PM MST Friday for AZZ537-540>546-
     548>551.

CA...Wind Advisory from 8 PM this evening to 2 PM PDT Friday for 
     CAZ564-565-568>570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Benedict
LONG TERM...Benedict 
AVIATION...RW
FIRE WEATHER...Benedict
